statement: a tool-call that writes a file under /etc via a server must not be admitted under mcp's permit (sem: SEM-gx-gate-353)
why:
the mcp-side one of **M7 hand 4 (H-9's 'linkage to pack shipping')**, and the most load-bearing line in this suite: **the very `/etc/passwd` that FA-1/FA-2 refuse on the fs substrate must not become admittable simply by changing the substrate**. The fs pack's rule reaches only fs locators, and a transformation reaching the same file via an MCP server is a different `SubstrateKind`, a different locator, a different policy subject. `policies/mcp/deny-etc-resources.cedar` shipped to close that hole, and this vector is the negative-case measurement that it is closed.

The control (`file:///srv/notes.md`) changes **only** the resource's path -- not one character differs in the server or the scheme. ∴ what separates this pair is only the forbid's pattern.

🔴 If the pattern's anchor (`*#file:///etc/*`) were dropped, even a **normal** call to a server-side endpoint spelled `file:///etc` would fall to deny -- `crates/gx-gate/tests/ac_074.rs`'s mcp table holds that case by name. (sem: SEM-gx-gate-354)
